summary: Port reproduces the static double-rainbow hue map and overall brightness exactly, but draws ~5 wide bands where the original draws ~9 narrow ones, and its band wave travels the opposite way at ~1.8x the speed.
observations: Rig is a 60-px strip; neither side exposes any control (probe: 'no settable controls' on both), no compile or runtime errors, both alive and steady over 240 s.

Hue is FIXED per pixel on both sides and never changes with time: measured hue at every pixel over a 60 s window is 0,12,24,...,348 repeating twice across the strip (two full rainbows), identical orig vs port to within 1 degree. Colour reproduction is exact — the animation is purely a brightness envelope over that static rainbow.

STRUCTURE (main finding): dominant spatial frequency of the brightness envelope, measured per-frame by spatial DFT, is 9 bands/strip on the original and 5 (occasionally 6) on the port, stable on every frame across the whole 60 s window. Band pitch is therefore ~6.7 px (orig) vs ~11-12 px (port) — the port's bright bands and its black gaps are ~1.6x too wide and there are ~1.8x too few of them. Visible directly in the luminance profiles: at t=0 the original's dark gaps sit near px 4-5, 12-13, 18-20, 25-27, 33-34, 39-40, 47-49, 53-55 (8 gaps), the port's near px 6-11, 18-21, 28-33, 39-44, 52-55 (5 wide gaps).

The band count scales with pixel count on BOTH sides the same way — bands are a fixed number of PIXELS, not a fixed fraction of the strip: orig 4 / 9 / 17 bands at 30 / 60 / 120 px (pitch ~7 px), port 3 / 5.5 / 11 bands (pitch ~11 px). So the ratio is a constant ~1.6x error, not a resolution-handling difference. The hue map by contrast IS normalised on both (always exactly two rainbows across the strip at 30, 60 and 120 px).

MOTION (second main finding): tracking the phase of the dominant spatial component frame by frame over 60 s, the original's band wave advances monotonically toward INCREASING pixel index at +0.68 px/s (+37.3 px in 55 s); the port's advances monotonically toward DECREASING pixel index at -1.20 px/s (-65.8 px in 55 s). Directions are opposite and the port is ~1.8x faster in px/s.

The temporal band-to-band cycle is nearly identical on both — one full band pitch takes 9.88 s on the original and 10.0 s on the port — so the speed difference is entirely a consequence of the wider band pitch, not a different time constant.

In the waterfalls this reads as: original = clean, evenly spaced diagonal streaks all leaning the SAME way for the whole 240 s survey; port = a zigzag / chevron weave, because a weaker rightward 9-band component (measured at +0.66 px/s, i.e. the original's wave, present in the port at ~40% of the dominant amplitude) interferes with the dominant leftward 5-band wave the original does not have.

GLOBAL PERIOD: full-frame autocorrelation over 60 s gives an exact recurrence at 49.2 s for the original (mean abs diff 1.9/255, with weaker near-repeats every 9.84 s) and at 30.0 s for the port (diff 2.6/255, near-repeats every 10.0 s). The original's loop is ~5 sub-cycles long, the port's only ~3 — the port repeats itself 1.6x sooner.

Whole-strip brightness averages match (orig meanBrightness avg 74.7, port 75.8) and motion energy matches exactly (both avg 7.6, max 10-11 at 5 fps), but the port's strip mean swings wider: 59-93 vs the original's 68-83 over 60 s — the expected consequence of fewer, wider bands.

Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): cumulative drift measured at 2, 5, 20 and 40 fps agrees to within 0.2 px over 50 s on each side, and the `motion` stat scales as 1/fps on both. No frame-rate coupling on either side.
Both sides are fully deterministic: seed 1234 produces byte-identical statsSummary to seed 1 on both. No RNG character to compare.

Steady state is fine on both: a --skip 120 window is statistically indistinguishable from the opening window (orig mean 74.2, port 75.8, both brightnessTrend steady, zeroMotionFrames 0). Nothing dies or saturates.
feedback: Colour is already perfect — the static per-pixel hue map (two full rainbows across the strip, hue = 12 deg per pixel at 60 px, never varying with time) matches the original exactly. Do not touch it.

Fix the band pitch: the original packs 9 bright bands into a 60-px strip (~6.7 px pitch, and 4 bands at 30 px / 17 at 120 px, so the pitch is in PIXELS not in strip fractions). The port packs 5 (~11-12 px pitch, 3 at 30 px / 11 at 120 px). The port's spatial frequency of the brightness envelope is ~0.6x what it should be — scale it up by ~1.65x so the dominant spatial DFT bin reads 9 on a 60-px strip.
Reverse the band wave's direction: the original's bands crawl toward increasing pixel index, the port's toward decreasing. Flip the sign of whatever advances the brightness envelope's spatial phase.

Do NOT change the time constant while fixing the above: both sides already take ~10 s for a band to advance one full band pitch (orig 9.88 s, port 10.0 s). Once the pitch is corrected to ~6.7 px the px/s speed drops from 1.20 to ~0.68 automatically, which is the original's value.

The port carries a second, weaker brightness component at the ORIGINAL's spatial frequency (9 bands/strip) travelling at the original's +0.66 px/s, at about 40% of its dominant amplitude. The original has no counterpart travelling the other way. The zigzag/chevron weave visible in the port's 60 s and 240 s waterfalls is these two counter-travelling waves beating; the original's waterfall is a single family of parallel diagonals. Removing or correcting the spurious wide leftward wave should remove the chevrons.

Lengthen the overall loop: the original repeats exactly every 49.2 s (about five 9.84 s sub-cycles), the port every 30.0 s (three 10.0 s sub-cycles). Whatever secondary modulation sets how many sub-cycles pass before the frame repeats is one step short of the original's — target a 5:1 ratio of global period to band-cycle period, not 3:1.

Verified as already correct and not needing attention: mean brightness (74.7 vs 75.8), motion energy (7.6 both), fps-invariance, determinism across seeds, steady state out to 240 s, and the absence of controls on both sides. The port's slightly wider strip-mean brightness swing (59-93 vs 68-83) should self-correct once the band count is fixed.
